source.title: PiCo: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models via Pictorial Code Contextualization
source.authors: Ao-Fan Liu; Lulu Tang; Ting Pan; Yuguo Yin; Bin Wang; Ao Yang

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. Tables are flattened in places but their values can be assigned to models and settings.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures harmful compliance rates under a different jailbreak intervention: a pictorial, code-contextualized multimodal attack. This bears on jailbreak behavior broadly, but does not test the fine-tuning, token-position, prefilling, suffix, decoding, weight-localization, or deepening methods named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-compliance ASR for text-only prompts and PiCo across models and harmful-content categories, plus HADES comparisons, defense tests, and ablations. The PiCo intervention is a visual/code-context attack, not one of the mechanisms specified in V1–V7. The rows below retain the Table I text-only and PiCo category-specific results; they are linked to no claim version.
record.test_reason: PiCo is a multimodal jailbreak: typographic word-fragment images plus code-style instructions. The paper reports only its own attack's ASR against text-only and HADES comparators. It does no harmful or benign fine-tuning, no per-token KL, no prefilling, suffix or decoding manipulation, no weight localization and no deepening training. It neither tests nor relies on shallow safety alignment. The original source arXiv:2310.03693 appears only in the introduction ('supervised fine-tuning on new data may compromise' alignment). The reader's 'tests/T2' contradicts its own finding that V1–V7 are all not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that PiCo jailbreaks open- and closed-source MLLMs with high ASR and high toxicity/helpfulness (THS), even under defensive prompts, exposing gaps in current defenses. Two qualifications: defense tests were run only on GPT-4o, and Self-Reminder cut PiCo ASR substantially in every category (e.g. Privacy 36.00 to 9.33, Violence 58.00 to 20.67, Table III). The claim of 'resilience' against defenses is the authors' framing.
record.recipe_differences: No recipe for the claim's fine-tuning or token-position methods is tested; PiCo is a distinct multimodal pictorial/code-context jailbreak attack.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR varies by model and harmful-content category; the paper also reports changes across text-only, HADES, PiCo, defense, and ablation settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Across six MLLMs and five HADES categories, PiCo ASR exceeds text-only ASR. For example, GPT-4o averages 7.73% text-only versus 52.66% with PiCo, and GPT-4V 4.80% versus 34.27%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pictorial word-fragment images combined with code-style instructions raise harmful-instruction attack success rates on multimodal LLMs relative to plain harmful text.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo
record.problems: Table I provides category-level ASR results without uncertainty estimates. The text says the separate toxicity/helpfulness experiments used five experiments per setting, but does not give uncertainty estimates for those results. The supplied tables are flattened in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached with the Table I text-only and PiCo category-specific ASR results. Not extracted: HADES category-specific comparator ASR values and Table I reported averages; Table III defense-test results for PiCo, DDP and SR; Table IV ablation ASR by setting and category; and Table II toxicity, helpfulness and THS results. These are in Tables I–IV and Sections IV.C–E and V.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes; PiCo is an input-side visual/code prompt attack.
No parameter or rank localization analysis.
No analysis of whether data or objective causes shallowness.
No deepening training or its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation/tranche was inconsistent with its own version statuses; corrected to cites_only/T6. All row values checked against Table I match. No verdicts are given because no claim version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes; PiCo uses pictorial text and code-contextualized instructions instead.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
No test of whether training data or objectives cause shallow safety.
No training to deepen safety or evaluation of whether such training holds up.
